title: Indian Students Keep Heading Abroad Despite Tighter Visa Rules Across the Big Four Destinations
excerpt: F-1 issuances to Indians fell 60%, Canada's rejection rate hit 80%, and Australia doubled post-study work fees — yet outbound student numbers continue to rise as families recalculate rather than retreat.
body:
• Indian student enrolment in the U.S. fell 6.9% to 352,644 as of February 2026, according to the Department of Homeland Security's SEVIS data shared in India's Parliament.
  • F-1 student visa issuances to Indians dropped more than 60% between May and August 2025 compared to the same period in 2024, with July-August alone seeing a nearly 80% decline.
  • Canada's study permit rejection rate for Indian applicants reached 80% in 2025, while Australia doubled its post-study work visa fee to AUD $4,600.
  • Despite these barriers, Indian undergraduate applications to UK universities rose 6.9% in 2026, and alternative destinations like Germany, Ireland, and New Zealand are gaining ground.

The U.S. Pullback

More than 3.5 lakh Indian students are pursuing education in the United States as of February 2026 — a decline of 6.9% from 378,787 the previous year, India's Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh told the Rajya Sabha in a written reply, citing data from the U.S. Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS), The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

https://x.com/NewsMeter_In/status/2091453282124435808

The decline reflects a convergence of policy changes. Between May and August 2025, F-1 visa issuances to Indian students fell more than 60% year-over-year, according to a Chronicle of Higher Education analysis of State Department data, as cited by Collegedunia. In July and August alone, the drop was nearly 80%.

The Trump administration suspended visa interviews at U.S. consulates for nearly a month in May 2025, creating backlogs that disrupted the entire summer intake cycle. Thousands of student visas were revoked in early 2025 amid broader immigration enforcement. A four-year cap on student visa duration replaced the previous "duration of status" system, and the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme — the primary financial rationale for Indian STEM students — faces proposed reform or termination.

"Without OPT, students will have to leave immediately after their study program because potential recruiter organisations will be wary to pay $100,000 for a fresh graduate over and above their regular compensation."

— Suchindra Kumar, Partner, PwC India Education Sector

Canada, UK, and Australia Tighten in Parallel

Canada, the fastest-growing destination for Indian students between 2019 and 2023, has reversed sharply. Study permits for Indian nationals dropped 50% in 2025. Canada capped 2026 study permit issuances at 408,000 — down from over one million active permit holders in January 2024. The rejection rate for Indian applicants reached 80%, according to GradRight data cited by Collegedunia.

The UK is trimming its Graduate Route visa from two years to 18 months for students graduating from January 2027. From January 2025, only PhD and research-based postgraduate students can bring dependents. English language and financial proof thresholds have been raised.

Australia's cost escalation has been the steepest in raw terms. On March 1, 2026, the application fee for the Temporary Graduate Visa (Subclass 485) doubled to AUD $4,600 — the third increase in just over a year. The student visa fee now stands at AUD $2,000, the most expensive study visa fee of any major destination globally.

Why Students Are Not Stopping

The tightening has not halted outbound mobility — it has redirected it. Indian undergraduate applications to UK universities rose 6.9% in the 2026 admissions cycle, reaching 17,250, according to UCAS figures. A total of 90,425 sponsored study visas were granted to Indians in the year ending March 2026, making them the largest group among international students in the UK.

Germany, Ireland, and New Zealand are absorbing students who might previously have defaulted to the Big Four. Germany charges no tuition at public universities and offers 18 months of post-study work rights. Ireland, English-speaking and home to major tech headquarters, offers two years. New Zealand announced a new Short-Term Graduate Work Visa from late 2026, and Indian enrolments there grew 99% in 2023 and 49% in 2024.

The ROI Calculation Has Changed

For Indian families, the study-abroad decision has always been framed as an investment. When post-study work rights are cut, fees doubled, and rejection rates approach 80%, the expected return on a Rs 50-80 lakh commitment shrinks. PwC India's Suchindra Kumar notes that of the 4 lakh students who emigrate for studies annually, no more than 10-15% travel for strictly educational purposes — the rest are calculating employment pathways that are now less certain, Livemint reported.

What Students Should Do

Immigration advisors recommend applying at least four to six months before intended start dates, verifying post-study work eligibility before choosing a programme, and researching backup destinations in parallel rather than as an afterthought. The landscape has changed materially from even two years ago, and financial planning based on 2022-2023 figures no longer reflects reality.
image_caption: An Indian Institute of Technology campus. Despite tightening visa rules across the US, UK, Canada, and Australia, the number of Indian students choosing to study overseas continues to grow.
nri_angle: Indian families spending Rs 50-80 lakh on overseas degrees are recalculating ROI as every major destination simultaneously tightens visa rules, post-study work rights, and costs.
